description: Manage a freelance client from first inquiry through project delivery and final payment.

steps.description: Receive and qualify an inbound client inquiry.

inputs.name: inquiry-details
inputs.desc: The client's message, form submission, or referral context

inputs.name: service-offerings
inputs.desc: List of services offered with pricing ranges

outputs.name: inquiry-summary
outputs.desc: Structured summary of what the client needs

outputs.name: qualification-score
outputs.desc: Fit assessment based on budget, timeline, and scope

process: Extract the client's name, company, project description, budget range, and timeline from the inquiry.
Score the inquiry against your qualification criteria (budget fit, scope match, availability, strategic interest).
If the inquiry passes the threshold, draft a response proposing a discovery call with available times.
If it does not pass, draft a polite decline with a referral suggestion.

steps.description: Conduct a discovery call to understand the client's needs and assess project fit.

outputs.name: discovery-notes
outputs.desc: Structured notes from the discovery call covering goals, constraints, and success criteria

outputs.name: project-scope-draft
outputs.desc: Draft scope including deliverables, timeline estimate, and budget range

process: Prepare the call agenda: client goals, current situation, success criteria, budget, timeline, decision process.
During the call, document answers to each agenda item and note any red flags (scope creep risk, unclear decision maker, unrealistic timeline).
After the call, summarize the project scope, deliverables, timeline, and estimated budget.
Decide whether to proceed with a proposal or decline the engagement.

steps.description: Write a project proposal based on discovery findings.

outputs.name: project-proposal
outputs.desc: The complete proposal including scope, approach, timeline, deliverables, pricing, and terms

outputs.name: pricing-breakdown
outputs.desc: Itemized pricing by deliverable or phase

process: Write the problem statement and objectives in the client's language, reflecting what they said in discovery.
Define the approach, methodology, and phases of work.
List the deliverables with acceptance criteria for each.
Set the timeline with milestones and the pricing structure (fixed, hourly, milestone-based).
Include the terms: payment schedule, revision policy, cancellation clause, IP ownership.

steps.description: Negotiate and finalize the contract with the client.

inputs.name: project-proposal
inputs.desc: The proposal sent to the client

outputs.name: signed-contract
outputs.desc: The executed contract or agreement

outputs.name: payment-schedule
outputs.desc: Agreed payment milestones and amounts

process: Send the proposal and allow time for client review.
Address client questions and requested changes, tracking each revision.
Negotiate any changes to scope, pricing, or terms, ensuring each change is reflected in the contract.
Finalize and execute the contract (e-signature or countersigned PDF).
Confirm the payment schedule and method.

steps.description: Onboard the client after contract signing: set up communication, access, and project tools.

outputs.name: onboarding-checklist
outputs.desc: Completed checklist of onboarding steps

outputs.name: project-workspace
outputs.desc: Links and access details for the shared project workspace

process: Send the welcome email with the project timeline, key contacts, and what you need from the client.
Set up the shared workspace (project management tool, file sharing, communication channel).
Schedule the kickoff meeting and recurring check-ins.
Collect any materials, credentials, or assets needed from the client.
Confirm the client has access to all shared tools and understands the communication protocol.

steps.description: Execute the project by tracking progress against milestones and managing deliverables.

outputs.name: milestone-status
outputs.desc: Status of each milestone (not started, in progress, complete, blocked)

outputs.name: deliverables-log
outputs.desc: Record of deliverables submitted and client feedback received

process: Break the project into milestones with clear deliverables and due dates.
Track progress against each milestone, updating the client at the agreed cadence.
Submit deliverables for client review at each milestone and document their feedback.
Handle revision requests within the scope of the contract.
Flag any risks to the timeline or budget early and propose mitigation.

steps.description: Deliver the final work, collect payment, and close out the project.

inputs.name: deliverables-log
inputs.desc: Record of all deliverables and feedback

outputs.name: final-deliverable-package
outputs.desc: All final deliverables, files, and documentation handed to the client

outputs.name: project-closeout-record
outputs.desc: Record of the completed project including final invoice, payment confirmation, and client feedback

process: Submit the final deliverables and get client sign-off.
Transfer all files, credentials, and assets to the client per the contract.
Send the final invoice and confirm payment.
Request a testimonial or referral if the engagement went well.
Archive the project files and update your portfolio.

description: Track billable time against projects and generate invoices from the tracked hours.

steps.description: Set up the time tracking system for a project or client.

inputs.name: project-details
inputs.desc: Project name, client, billing rate, and budget

inputs.name: billing-structure
inputs.desc: Hourly, daily, or milestone-based billing terms

outputs.name: tracking-configuration
outputs.desc: Configured time tracking categories, rates, and budget limits

outputs.name: tracking-tool-access
outputs.desc: Access details for the time tracking tool

process: Create the project in the time tracking tool with the correct billing rate and budget cap.
Set up task categories that match the project phases or deliverables.
Configure alerts for budget thresholds (50%, 75%, 90%).
Document the tracking protocol (minimum entry granularity, description requirements, daily entry deadline).

steps.description: Log time entries against projects and tasks on a daily basis.

outputs.name: time-entries
outputs.desc: Logged time entries with date, hours, task, and description

outputs.name: running-total
outputs.desc: Running total of hours and billable amount for the period

process: At the end of each work session, log the time entry with the date, duration, task category, and a brief description of the work done.
Review entries against the project budget to check utilization.
Flag any non-billable time separately (admin, internal meetings, rework).
Verify that descriptions are specific enough for the client to understand the work performed.

steps.description: Review time entries for accuracy and completeness before invoicing.

inputs.name: time-entries
inputs.desc: Raw time entries for the billing period

outputs.name: verified-entries
outputs.desc: Reviewed and corrected time entries ready for invoicing

outputs.name: period-summary
outputs.desc: Summary of hours by task, billable vs non-billable, and total amount

process: Pull all entries for the billing period and check for missing days or gaps.
Verify that each entry has a clear description and correct task assignment.
Correct any duplicate or miscategorized entries.
Calculate the period total and compare against the budget or retainer allocation.

steps.description: Generate an invoice from verified time entries.

outputs.name: invoice-document
outputs.desc: The generated invoice with line items, amounts, and payment terms

outputs.name: invoice-number
outputs.desc: Unique invoice identifier

process: Create the invoice with your business details, client details, invoice number, and date.
List the line items (hours by task or phase, rate, and subtotal for each).
Add any expenses or fixed-fee items.
Include the payment terms (net 15, net 30), accepted payment methods, and late payment policy.
Review the invoice for accuracy before sending.

steps.description: Send the invoice and track payment status.

outputs.name: payment-status
outputs.desc: Current payment status (sent, viewed, paid, overdue)

outputs.name: billing-record
outputs.desc: Record of the invoice, send date, payment date, and amount received

process: Send the invoice to the client via the agreed method (email, invoicing platform).
Log the send date and payment due date.
Monitor for payment receipt and match against the invoice amount.
If payment is overdue, send a reminder at the agreed intervals (3 days, 7 days, 14 days).
Record the final payment date and amount, and note any discrepancies.

description: Manage a retainer agreement: track utilization, report to the client, and handle renewals.

steps.description: Define the retainer terms including hours, scope, rollover rules, and reporting.

inputs.name: client-needs
inputs.desc: What the client needs on an ongoing basis

inputs.name: proposed-terms
inputs.desc: Proposed hours per month, rate, and scope

outputs.name: retainer-agreement
outputs.desc: The retainer terms document covering hours, rate, scope, rollover, and reporting

outputs.name: tracking-setup
outputs.desc: How hours will be tracked and reported

process: Define the monthly hour allocation and billing rate.
Specify what is in scope and what requires a separate engagement.
Set the rollover rules (do unused hours carry forward, and for how long).
Define the reporting cadence and format (weekly summary, monthly utilization report).
Specify the renewal terms (auto-renew, notice period, rate adjustment window).

steps.description: Track hours used against the retainer allocation each month.

outputs.name: utilization-data
outputs.desc: Hours used, hours remaining, and percentage utilized for the current period

outputs.name: work-log
outputs.desc: Itemized log of work performed under the retainer

process: Log all retainer work with the date, hours, and description.
Calculate the running utilization against the monthly allocation.
Alert the client when utilization reaches 75% and 90% of the allocation.
Track any rollover hours from prior months separately.

steps.description: Produce the monthly utilization report for the client.

outputs.name: monthly-report
outputs.desc: The utilization report showing hours used, work performed, and hours remaining

outputs.name: recommendations
outputs.desc: Suggestions for adjusting the retainer based on utilization patterns

process: Summarize the hours used by category or project area.
Compare utilization to the prior three months to identify trends.
If consistently over or under the allocation, recommend an adjustment.
Include a brief narrative of the work performed and any upcoming priorities.

steps.description: Handle situations where retainer hours are exceeded or scope changes are needed.

outputs.name: overage-resolution
outputs.desc: How the overage was handled (additional billing, scope adjustment, or hours added)

outputs.name: updated-terms
outputs.desc: Any changes to the retainer terms

process: When hours are exceeded, notify the client with the overage amount and cause.
Propose options: bill the overage at the agreed rate, add hours to the retainer, or reduce scope.
Get client approval for the chosen resolution.
Update the retainer tracking and terms if the allocation changes.

steps.description: Review and renew or adjust the retainer at the end of the period.

inputs.name: overage-resolution
inputs.desc: Any overage resolutions from the period

outputs.name: renewal-decision
outputs.desc: Whether the retainer is renewed, adjusted, or ended

outputs.name: retainer-record
outputs.desc: Complete record of the retainer period including utilization, payments, and outcomes

process: Review the full period's utilization, overages, and client satisfaction.
Propose renewal terms based on actual usage patterns.
Negotiate any rate or scope changes for the next period.
Execute the renewal agreement or close out the retainer.
Archive the period record.

description: Handle scope changes on an active project: assess impact, write the change order, and update the plan.

steps.description: Receive and document a scope change request from the client.

inputs.name: change-description
inputs.desc: What the client is requesting to add, remove, or modify

inputs.name: current-project-plan
inputs.desc: The current project scope, timeline, and budget

outputs.name: change-request-record
outputs.desc: Documented change request with description, requester, date, and priority

outputs.name: initial-assessment
outputs.desc: Quick assessment of whether the change is minor, moderate, or major

process: Document the change request in writing, even if it came verbally.
Clarify the request with the client to ensure you understand what they want.
Classify the change as minor (within existing scope flexibility), moderate (requires timeline or budget adjustment), or major (requires contract amendment).
Acknowledge receipt and set expectations for when the impact assessment will be ready.

steps.description: Assess the impact of the scope change on timeline, budget, and deliverables.

outputs.name: impact-analysis
outputs.desc: Detailed analysis of how the change affects timeline, budget, and other deliverables

outputs.name: options-list
outputs.desc: Options for accommodating the change (with tradeoffs for each)

process: Estimate the additional hours or effort required.
Identify any deliverables that will be delayed or affected.
Calculate the cost impact at the current billing rate.
Identify at least two options: absorb the change with tradeoffs, or add time and budget.
Document the risks of each option.

steps.description: Write the formal change order for client approval.

outputs.name: change-order
outputs.desc: The change order document specifying the change, cost, timeline adjustment, and terms

outputs.name: revised-schedule
outputs.desc: Updated project schedule reflecting the change

process: Write the change order with a clear description of what changes, the cost adjustment, and the new timeline.
Reference the original contract and the specific sections being amended.
Include a signature line for client approval.
Attach the revised schedule showing the impact on milestones.

steps.description: Get client approval on the change order and update the project plan.

outputs.name: approved-change
outputs.desc: The signed change order

outputs.name: updated-project-plan
outputs.desc: The project plan updated with the approved change

process: Present the change order to the client with the impact analysis.
Answer questions and negotiate if needed.
Get the client's written approval (signature, email confirmation, or platform approval).
Update the project plan, budget tracker, and timeline with the approved changes.
Communicate the updated plan to anyone else on the project team.

description: Set up a new consulting engagement from structure definition through kickoff.

steps.description: Define the engagement structure and billing model.

inputs.name: client-objectives
inputs.desc: What the client wants to achieve

outputs.name: engagement-model
outputs.desc: The engagement structure (fixed-fee, T&M, retainer, milestone-based) with rationale

outputs.name: resource-plan
outputs.desc: Who will work on the engagement, their roles, and allocation

process: Assess the client's objectives, risk tolerance, and budget certainty to select the billing model.
For fixed-fee: define the deliverables and price. For T&M: set the rate card and estimate. For retainer: set the monthly allocation. For milestone: define the phases and payments.
Identify the team members, their roles, and their time allocation.
Document the rationale for the chosen structure.

steps.description: Write the statement of work for the engagement.

inputs.name: engagement-model
inputs.desc: The engagement structure and billing model

outputs.name: statement-of-work
outputs.desc: The SOW covering scope, deliverables, timeline, team, pricing, and terms

outputs.name: acceptance-criteria
outputs.desc: Criteria for accepting each deliverable

process: Write the background and objectives section in the client's language.
Define the scope of work with explicit inclusions and exclusions.
List each deliverable with its acceptance criteria and due date.
Specify the team, their roles, and the governance structure (who approves what).
Include the pricing, payment schedule, assumptions, and change management process.

steps.description: Set up the project tools and communication channels for the engagement.

outputs.name: tool-inventory
outputs.desc: List of tools, platforms, and channels set up for the engagement

outputs.name: access-roster
outputs.desc: Who has access to what, with login details shared securely

process: Set up the project management tool with the engagement phases, milestones, and tasks.
Create the shared document repository with the folder structure.
Set up the communication channel (Slack channel, Teams group, or email list).
Share access with the client team and your team, using secure methods for credentials.
Document the tool inventory and access roster.

steps.description: Establish the reporting cadence and templates for the engagement.

outputs.name: reporting-schedule
outputs.desc: Calendar of status reports, reviews, and steering committee meetings

outputs.name: report-templates
outputs.desc: Templates for status reports, milestone reviews, and risk logs

process: Define the reporting frequency (weekly status, biweekly review, monthly steering).
Create templates for each report type with the required sections.
Schedule the recurring meetings and send calendar invites.
Assign report ownership (who writes, who reviews, who receives).

steps.description: Conduct the engagement kickoff meeting with the client.

outputs.name: kickoff-minutes
outputs.desc: Minutes from the kickoff meeting including decisions and action items

outputs.name: engagement-setup-record
outputs.desc: Complete record of the engagement setup (SOW, tools, reporting, kickoff)

process: Present the engagement overview: objectives, scope, team, timeline, and governance.
Walk through the communication plan and reporting cadence.
Confirm roles, responsibilities, and escalation paths.
Capture action items and assign owners with due dates.
Distribute the kickoff minutes and confirm the engagement is officially underway.

description: Create a portfolio case study from a completed project to demonstrate your work.

steps.description: Select a project for the case study and get client permission.

inputs.name: completed-projects
inputs.desc: List of completed projects with outcomes

inputs.name: portfolio-gaps
inputs.desc: What your current portfolio is missing (industries, services, outcomes)

outputs.name: selected-project
outputs.desc: The project selected for the case study with rationale

outputs.name: client-permission
outputs.desc: Written permission from the client to use the project in your portfolio

process: Review completed projects and rank by strength of results, relevance to target clients, and visual appeal.
Identify which project fills the biggest gap in your current portfolio.
Contact the client and request permission to feature the project, specifying what you will share.
If the client declines naming, agree on an anonymized version (industry and results without the company name).

steps.description: Write the case study content following the challenge, approach, solution, results structure.

outputs.name: case-study-draft
outputs.desc: Written case study with challenge, approach, solution, and results sections

outputs.name: metrics-summary
outputs.desc: Quantified results and before/after comparisons

process: Write the challenge section: what the client was dealing with before the engagement.
Write the approach section: what methodology you used and why.
Write the solution section: what you built or delivered.
Write the results section: measurable outcomes, before and after metrics, and client feedback.
Keep the language factual and let the numbers do the talking.

steps.description: Design the visual presentation of the case study.

outputs.name: case-study-final
outputs.desc: The designed case study ready for publication

outputs.name: case-study-assets
outputs.desc: Images, screenshots, charts, and pull quotes for promotion

process: Design the layout with sections for challenge, approach, solution, and results.
Add visuals: before/after screenshots, process diagrams, or data charts.
Highlight the key metric in a pull-out stat block.
Include a client testimonial if available.
Produce social-friendly image assets for promotion.

steps.description: Publish the case study and promote it across channels.

outputs.name: published-url
outputs.desc: URL of the published case study

outputs.name: promotion-record
outputs.desc: Record of where the case study was shared and the engagement it received

process: Publish the case study on your website or portfolio platform.
Share on LinkedIn, relevant communities, and in your email newsletter.
Tag the client (with permission) for additional reach.
Add the case study link to relevant proposal templates and pitch decks.

description: Source, onboard, manage, and pay subcontractors on a project.

steps.description: Identify the skills and capacity needed from a subcontractor.

inputs.name: project-requirements
inputs.desc: The project scope and deliverables requiring outside help

inputs.name: skill-gaps
inputs.desc: Skills or capacity you lack for this project

outputs.name: sub-role-definition
outputs.desc: Description of the role, skills, deliverables, and time commitment needed

outputs.name: budget-allocation
outputs.desc: Budget available for the subcontractor (rate range and total hours)

process: List the specific tasks or deliverables the subcontractor will handle.
Define the required skills, experience level, and any tool proficiency.
Estimate the hours and timeline for the subcontracted work.
Set the budget range based on market rates and your project margin.

steps.description: Source and vet potential subcontractors.

outputs.name: candidate-shortlist
outputs.desc: Vetted candidates with portfolio samples, rate, and availability

outputs.name: vetting-notes
outputs.desc: Notes from interviews, portfolio review, and reference checks

process: Source candidates from your network, freelance platforms, or referrals.
Review portfolios and work samples for quality and relevance.
Conduct a brief interview or trial task to assess fit.
Check references from prior clients or collaborators.
Select the top candidate based on skill, rate, availability, and reliability.

steps.description: Negotiate terms and sign the subcontractor agreement.

outputs.name: sub-agreement
outputs.desc: Signed subcontractor agreement covering scope, rate, IP, confidentiality, and payment terms

outputs.name: onboarding-plan
outputs.desc: Steps to onboard the subcontractor to the project

process: Draft the subcontractor agreement with scope, deliverables, rate, payment schedule, and timeline.
Include IP assignment, confidentiality, and non-solicitation clauses as needed.
Negotiate and finalize the terms.
Execute the agreement.

steps.description: Onboard the subcontractor to the project with context, tools, and expectations.

outputs.name: sub-workspace-access
outputs.desc: Tool access and communication channels set up for the subcontractor

outputs.name: deliverable-schedule
outputs.desc: Agreed schedule of deliverables with review points

process: Brief the subcontractor on the project context, client expectations, and their specific deliverables.
Grant access to the relevant project tools, files, and communication channels.
Set up the deliverable schedule with check-in points.
Clarify the review and feedback process.
Confirm the subcontractor has everything they need to start.

steps.description: Manage the subcontractor's deliverables, quality, and payment.

outputs.name: quality-review-log
outputs.desc: Record of deliverable reviews, feedback given, and revisions made

outputs.name: sub-payment-record
outputs.desc: Record of invoices received, payments made, and total cost

process: Review each deliverable against the acceptance criteria at each milestone.
Provide clear, actionable feedback for any revisions needed.
Process the subcontractor's invoices on the agreed schedule.
Track the total cost against the budget allocation.
At project end, archive the subcontractor's work and close out the agreement.

description: Write and deliver a consulting proposal from discovery through negotiation to close.

steps.description: Conduct the discovery session to understand the client's needs for the proposal.

inputs.name: prospect-context
inputs.desc: Background on the prospect (company, industry, known pain points)

inputs.name: engagement-type
inputs.desc: Type of engagement being considered (advisory, implementation, assessment, training)

outputs.name: discovery-findings
outputs.desc: Structured findings from the discovery session

outputs.name: success-criteria
outputs.desc: What the client will consider a successful engagement

process: Prepare the discovery questions tailored to the engagement type.
Conduct the session, focusing on: current state, desired state, obstacles, prior attempts, decision criteria, and timeline.
Document the findings in a structured format.
Confirm the success criteria with the client before leaving the session.

steps.description: Design the consulting approach and methodology for the proposal.

outputs.name: proposed-approach
outputs.desc: The methodology, phases, and activities for the engagement

outputs.name: effort-estimate
outputs.desc: Estimated effort by phase, role, and total

process: Select the methodology or framework that fits the client's situation.
Break the engagement into phases with clear activities and outputs for each.
Estimate the effort for each phase by role (partner, senior, analyst).
Identify the key assumptions and risks that could change the estimate.
Validate that the approach addresses each of the client's success criteria.

steps.description: Build the pricing for the proposal based on the approach and effort estimate.

outputs.name: pricing-model
outputs.desc: The pricing structure with total, phase breakdown, and payment schedule

outputs.name: value-justification
outputs.desc: How the pricing relates to the expected ROI or value delivered

process: Apply the rate card to the effort estimate to calculate the base price.
Decide whether to present as fixed-fee, T&M with a cap, or blended rate.
Structure the payment schedule aligned with milestones or phases.
Prepare the value justification linking the investment to the expected outcomes.
Set the discount or negotiation range if needed.

steps.description: Write the proposal document.

outputs.name: proposal-document
outputs.desc: The complete proposal document ready for presentation

outputs.name: executive-summary
outputs.desc: One-page executive summary for decision-makers

process: Write the executive summary: problem, approach, expected outcome, investment.
Write the full proposal sections: background, objectives, approach, team, timeline, deliverables, pricing, terms.
Add the firm's credentials and relevant case studies.
Design the document for readability (headers, white space, visual timeline).
Have a second set of eyes review for errors, tone, and completeness.

steps.description: Present the proposal to the client and handle negotiation.

outputs.name: client-decision
outputs.desc: The client's decision (accept, negotiate, decline) with any requested changes

outputs.name: proposal-record
outputs.desc: Complete record of the proposal process including all versions, client feedback, and final outcome

process: Present the proposal in a meeting (not just emailed), walking through the executive summary first.
Address questions and objections, documenting each one.
If the client requests changes, revise and resubmit within the agreed turnaround.
Once accepted, transition to contract and engagement setup.
If declined, ask for feedback and log the reason for future learning.
